changelog.entry: New: hover or focus an Invest button to see your funds after buying and after this season's heritage upkeep. A new Affordable in how many seasons? panel lists every adaptation tier and diversification level still ahead with how long they would take at your current income, and you can pin one target. Pin one personal goal (such as Keep 4 rows dry or Reach 200 population) under the investments and watch its bar fill; you get one ping when it is reached. The meters now count quiet seasons in a row without an acidity rise, with a star frame at 5 and 10. In the settlement panel, Roll a name picks a fun harbour name and writes it into the chronicle.

Investing in all three categories in one season now builds a balanced-seasons income streak (x1.1, x1.2, then x1.3 on that season's income); skipping a category breaks it. When three or more rows flood in one season it is called a Domino season, and adaptation costs 25% less for the next two seasons. Protect a heritage site when its row is about to flood and you get a SAVED! lifeboat moment and a chronicle entry. After each Advance Season a one-second report card shows funds, acidity and fish changes with arrows and the words good or watch (it is skipped with reduced motion). A Rewind button retracts your last Advance click once per run and marks the run with a tin hat. Finishing 20 seasons in Hard Lag with no Rewind and no checkpoint replay earns a gold anchor next to the title. Clicks and active seconds to the top adaptation tier are tracked, with your best kept in this browser and shown in the session summary. The storm forecast now shows a range with a chance to overtop your current seawalls and a small bell-curve chip with the wall height marked and labelled.

New: a line under the ocean acidity shows what acidity was three seasons ago and whether it is up, down or unchanged now, so the delay between what you did and what the fish feel is visible as numbers.

New: the Session Summary has a Copy result button that copies one line, such as Tide, 12 seasons, with your damage taken, damage saved by adaptation, adaptation tier and storms survived. Every achievement you have earned now has a Share button that copies a line you can paste anywhere, with the share of players who have it when that figure is available. The How to Play and Info panels link to the new Credits page.

New: a Season Planner (stage 3 to 5 seasons of investments and see projected acidity, fishing yield and dry rows at risk before spending anything, then commit the first season), a season scrubber under the coastline (drag back to see any earlier season's coast, meters, tier and heritage, read-only), a Session Library (save sessions in this browser and overlay any two on the graphs, one solid and one dashed), and a Harbor Almanac (lifetime seasons, rows kept dry, heritage protected and storms weathered, plus your best run for each sea scenario and lag mode, also shown in the session summary). The trend graphs gain a hover/tap/arrow-key crosshair with that season's numbers, a Last 10 / Last 20 / All range, and optional dash styles and point shapes per series. Every coastline tile can now be reached with the arrow keys.

New: a Harbor Ledger (every season as a sortable table with a small trend chart per column), Advance x5 (runs up to five quiet seasons and stops before a storm forecast, a fish-yield warning, a heritage site about to flood, or a monitoring crew becoming available again), game keys (A advance, X advance x5, 1/2/3 invest, R report, L ledger), filter chips and a search box for the full ticker history, a Copy as text button for your settlement summary, and a tab title that shows the season and any warning. Screen readers now hear each season's result and a row-by-row description of the coastline, and every panel you leave open stays open next time.

New Desktop layout for wide windows: a full-window view with the season, funds, acidity, fishing yield, sea level and damage as chips across the top, the coastline filling the screen with the live ticker under it, and your investments, Advance Season and coastal programmes in a column on the right. The status graphs, sea-level detail and then-vs-now coastline are windows opened from the Menu (Esc), and the sea-level scenario picker sits above the coastline. Pick it from the opening screen; your save carries over and the Classic layout is unchanged.
A faint glint now travels along a coastline held by the top-tier storm-surge barriers (motion only; off for reduced motion) (R-19).

Light theme polish: dimmed captions, the pale info bubble, the earned-achievement teal, the fishing warning banner and the selected feedback button were darkened for readable contrast on the light theme, and the coastline grid gets a visible edge. The land and flooded tiles themselves already passed. Dark mode is unchanged (Y11b).

Community seawall comparison: a line showing the median season other players first reached each seawall tier (sandbag berms, seawalls, reinforced seawalls, storm-surge barriers), shown only for tiers with enough data (D9).
Sister settlement: add a second, lower-lying coastal settlement that shares your funds and seawall tier but faces the sea harder (D3).
Achievement cards now show "Earned by N% of players" once enough real save data exists for that achievement (site-wide goal, Z1/Z27b).
Added a keyboard-shortcuts help overlay: press ? to see it, Esc to close it or whichever panel is open (site-wide goal, Z4).
Settings panel: added a "Reset to Default" button that resets text size and reduce-motion back to their defaults in one click (site-wide goal, folded from A26).

Session Summary is now print-friendly: printing the page (e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+P) while it's open hides the site chrome and renders the summary in clean dark-on-white, instead of the site's usual dark theme and UI.
Fixed a display bug where the Achievements panel showed as an empty box before its first open and never visually closed again once opened once.

Round-3 additions, all in collapsed panels: delayed-consequence timeline, a tide indicator, settlement name and chronicle, coastal heritage sites, citizen-science monitoring reports, opt-in storm seasons, managed retreat, population and displacement, economy diversification, and checkpoint replay with foresight.
D4: a small decorative wave cue next to the sea-level meter, speeding up as sea level rises — cosmetic only, doesn't change the meter's own numbers.
Z6: the personal-best label's "just improved" badge flash moved into the new shared shared/personal-best.css (also used by Canopy and Thaw) instead of a per-game copy of the same rule.

Round-2 pass: sea-level scenario select (conservative/moderate/severe), a seasons-survived counter, a fish-stock recovery celebration, worst-season cause, a suggested action on the fish-yield warning, live output-mix preview, dashed average and baseline markers on the acidity graph, a then-vs-now damage sparkline, per-tier seawall textures and a tier badge, and per-tile seasons-until-flood tooltips.
Output-mix dropdown (Fishing/Mixed/Industry) now states its acidity-rate and fish-crash trade-off directly in the option labels and a tooltip.
Settings panel added: text size (A-/A/A+) and a reduce-motion toggle, both persisted per-browser.

20 achievements added: investment milestones, all four adaptation tiers, coastline flood progression, the delayed fish-stock crash and recovery, and more — with an in-game panel, unlock toast, and hub link.

Post-launch pass (D1-D19): mobile action dock, a fourth adaptation tier (storm-surge barriers), a next-flood estimate, an expandable ticker history, a counterfactual "what if" replay, an end-of-session summary, a harder-lag difficulty mode, a fish-yield-crash early warning, and per-tile flood-threshold tooltips.
Space theme visual pass: starfield background, glass panels, gradient buttons — coastline land/flood colors kept exactly as they were.

Pass 3 (fun/teaching balance): added ticker narration for adaptation-tier unlocks and for the moment the damage curve visibly flattens, giving the payoff its own recovery narration alongside the existing fish-stock one.
Info Page added with curated real-world sources on ocean acidification and sea-level rise.
Pass 2: adaptation tech tree with per-tier dampening and a matching coastline seawall visual.
Pass 1: delayed-effect ticker log and a visually separate sea-level meter.
All 7 milestones complete: settlement loop, acidity meter + delayed fish-stock consequence, sea-level timeline, tile-grid coastline, hope-angle payoff, feedback prompt, visual pass + hub integration.
